findings.reason: the section would become a short citation of the implementing module and function rather than a design to build.
findings.text: §2's rule ("a run entering scoring dispatches its own review") is already implemented: the review reflex and its entry point exist at recovery.py:1156 (the comment "the reflex below runs the command instead of printing it"), recovery.py:2300 (`dispatch_review_for_run`) and recovery.py:4073 (`dispatch_awaiting_reviews`), so §2's premise that the composed command is only "printed instead of running" and that "Nothing creates it" is false at this revision — the plan should cite the landed owner and record the section as landed rather than re-specifying it

findings.reason: the section should cite plan_review.py and routing.py:2601 as its owners, which changes what a reviewer reads the section to be for.
findings.text: §3's rule ("a plan is not released until something has read it back; an unreviewed plan is refused for execution at dispatch") is already implemented: reckon/crew/plan_review.py owns the review record, its content fingerprint, the store and the finding-answer join, and reckon/crew/routing.py:2601 (`require_plan_reviewed`) is the dispatch preflight gate the posted decision "refuse-at-dispatch" describes, with landed answers already counted at plan_review.py:553 (`unanswered_findings`) — the plan does not name this module and presents the mechanism as new

findings.reason: §4 should name obligation_snapshot.py:809 as the owner of the age and confine itself to the obligation the plan actually owns (§6 already concedes the rendering elsewhere).
findings.text: §4's rule ("the actionable cells carry identity or age, not only a total") is already derived: obligation_snapshot.py:809 computes `oldest_age_seconds` for the summary and obligations.py:864 does the same, with reckon/crew/ticker.py:1932 already naming "how long the oldest member has waited" — the plan re-specifies a derivation that exists

findings.reason: §5 should extend the existing freshness reader and state what remains unsound in each of the five measured signals rather than re-describing a landed remedy.
findings.text: §5's "liveness signal keyed on freshness rather than on change" is already implemented: promotion.py:4351 (`_newest_stream_mtime`) and promotion.py:4360 ("the stream's newest mtime is polled until it has not advanced") is exactly a freshness-keyed liveness rule, with newest_stream at recovery.py:5947 and the process-liveness reader at claims.py:231 (`_worker_liveness`) behind it — the plan proposes the remedy without citing any of them

findings.reason: naming the existing inotify waiter and the supervisor's waitpid record turns §7 from a new subsystem into a bounded extension of them.
findings.text: §7 proposes "an optional completion signal the orchestrator can wait on" as new machinery, but a filesystem-event waiter already exists and is owned here: dispatch.py:3185 (`_inotify_descriptor`) and dispatch.py:3231 (`peer_read`, "block on filesystem events until a reply arrives") already implement "block on a watched directory for events", and the per-run supervisor already observes exit directly at dispatch.py:8138 (`os.waitpid(... WNOHANG)`) and dispatch.py:10151 (`_wait_status_record`) so the carrier for a finishing classification is already in flight — §7 should extend `peer_read`/`_inotify_descriptor` rather than add a parallel signal path

findings.reason: the plan should either extend the existing waiter or state why its contract cannot carry a completion classification.
findings.text: §7 adds a thin completion-signal layer over the existing event waiter with no justification for why that waiter cannot be extended, so the honest change (extend `peer_read` to carry a finishing classification, or have the supervisor write the classification it already computes) is not stated

findings.reason: the plan must name the owning module it extends or drop the derivation, otherwise two readers of the same fact drift.
findings.text: §4 and §5 both re-derive facts whose owners are named above (oldest-age at obligation_snapshot.py:809; freshness at promotion.py:4351) rather than extending them, and §6 hand-waves the duplication to `monitor-renders-what-it-is-given` while §4/§5 are declared sections of this plan

findings.reason: the section must account for the added CLI option and refusal family in its own text, or state why nothing can be retired.
findings.text: §3 adds to two of the four interface families without naming a retirement: the CLI option `--allow-unreviewed-plan` at cli.py:1794 and the refusal family `plan-review-missing` at cli.py:2119, and §7 proposes a further completion-signal option, while the section text names neither what these retire or merge

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3's plan-review store (reckon/crew/plan_review.py) hides the record shape, the content fingerprint, the store, the join and the decline recurrence behind a small interface, and §2 reuses the existing composer rather than wrapping it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 re-implements a filesystem-event wait rather than extending the existing inotify waiter, and §4/§5 re-derive an age and a freshness that named owners already compute.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 adds a CLI option and a refusal family and §7 adds a completion-signal option, and none of those sections names in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — four of the plan's five active mechanisms already exist at base (§2 recovery.py review reflex, §3 plan_review.py + routing.py gate, §4 obligation_snapshot.py oldest-age, §5 promotion.py/ recovery.py newest-stream freshness) and the plan presents each as still to be built.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §7 proposes an optional completion signal over machinery (the exchange that already blocks on filesystem events) without saying why that machinery cannot be extended instead.
